title: TurnProvenance
description: v2 (2026-07-29): what served one turn — read via GET /api/models/turns/<turn_id>/provenance, rendered as the per-turn detail the conversation surface reveals on demand (spec §4.5). Frozen in v2 because the spec promises per-turn inspectability and a promise with no interface cannot be implemented consistently: this file is where that promise says what it means. Distinct from resolution-event.schema.json, which is the account-wide 最近切换 feed keyed on state CHANGES; this is keyed on a TURN and always exists, switch or not. Storage is the implementing lane's decision, with one constraint: written when the turn resolves and readable after the process exits — 'which source paid for this turn' is a billing question the user asks days later. Same redaction invariant as every other payload here: ids and i18n keys, never credential material or raw upstream error bodies.

turn_id.description: The turn this describes, in whatever id space the session store already uses. Opaque here — this contract does not invent a new identifier.

ts.description: When the turn resolved (served or gave up), not when it started.

requested_model_id.description: What the caller asked for, as the caller-facing MENU identifier (prefixed for open menus) — before mapping. Recorded because 「我选的模型」 and 「实际跑的模型」 differing is precisely what the user is inspecting.

attempts.description: Every candidate this turn actually touched, in the order it touched them. A turn that switched mid-flight lists all of them, so the record EXPLAINS the switch instead of only naming the winner; a clean turn has exactly one entry. Candidates skipped before being tried (cooling, ineligible) are not attempts and are absent — the chain query answers 'what else exists'.

resolved_model_id.description: The id actually sent upstream for this attempt, mapping applied.

outcome.description: served = this attempt produced the turn's output. Exactly one attempt may be `served`, and it is always the last entry.

reason.description: Why a failed attempt failed, from the resolution-event `reason` vocabulary (quota_exhausted, rate_limited, server_error, network, credential_expired, credential_revoked, balance_exhausted, account_banned). null iff outcome = served.

served.description: Convenience projection of the `served` attempt, so the common render needs no array walk. NULL when every attempt failed — a turn that produced no output still has provenance, which is the point: the user asks what went wrong precisely then.
